narrative_purpose: Shows the same clearing twice, day and night, so temporal niche partitioning reads instantly: not two forests but one forest with two workforces, sharing the ground and never meeting.
subject: A single Pandoran clearing rendered twice as two stacked horizontal panels of identical geography - the same trunks, the same fallen log, the same rock. In the upper panel, daylight: a large winged flier banking above the canopy gap, a six-legged grazer browsing low undergrowth, a slender long-limbed arboreal animal in the branches. In the lower panel, the same clearing at night with the ground glowing: a pack of three six-legged predators moving across the open, a heavy solitary armoured predator with long sensory quills at the treeline, and a small lizard-like animal on a trunk with a spread luminous fan-membrane.
scene: Identical clearings, one lit from above and one lit from below, matched exactly in layout so the eye can hold them as the same place.
camera: The same fixed wide three-quarter view for both panels, no change in vantage between them.
light: Upper panel in cool diffuse overhead daylight with soft shadows; lower panel unlit from above, everything uplit in cyan and violet from the glowing floor.
palette: Upper panel cool grey-teal daylight with muted amber accents; lower panel void-indigo and cyan with faint violet; the two panels sharing one restrained palette.
style: Painterly naturalist comparison plate, hand-painted texture, deliberately matched staging between panels.
detail_level: Crisp on all six animals so each is identifiable; the shared background rendered identically and slightly softer in both panels.
composition: Two full-width horizontal panels stacked with a thin dark division, matched geography, animals spread across each so none overlaps its counterpart above or below, 4:3 overall.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette. The pack predators, grazer and flier must match their appearance in the chapter cover and the shift-change plate.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon or anime style
